problems.stem: A feedback template line reads 'Tighten this up before final.' Which rewrite makes it drive a design revision?
options: Frame 4's narration states the goal but not the learner action; add one sentence naming what the learner does here.
This is a bit confusing, can you clarify?
Tighten this up and also fix the fonts and headings.
problems.explanation: The strong line names a criterion, locates it in the draft, and requests an observable next move.

problems.stem: Which template line is praise rather than actionable feedback?
options: On slide 2, align the heading to the stated objective about navigation.
Add alt text to the diagram on slide 5.
Cut the second paragraph; it repeats the goal statement.
problems.explanation: Encouragement names no criterion, location, or action, so it cannot guide a revision.

problems.stem: An instructor uses AI to help draft comments on 12 design drafts. What is the strongest boundary?
options: Let the AI generate and post all 12 comment sets unedited.
Use AI to draft candidate criterion-located-action lines, then keep or cut each against the actual draft.
Refuse to use AI even for phrasing.
Ask AI only to make the comments sound more encouraging.
problems.explanation: AI proposes phrasing; the instructor's judgment against the real draft decides what stays.

problems.stem: Students keep revising only cosmetics. The template lists six equal-weight comments per draft. What is the best fix?
options: Add more comments so nothing is missed.
Cap the template at one prioritized revision per draft so the feedback itself does not overload the student.
Remove all comments and let students self-assess.
problems.explanation: Too many equal-weight comments hide the priority; one prioritized revision keeps feedback load on the design decision.
